record.paper_title: On chromatic numbers of space-times: open problems
record.original_question: For Minkowski space-time R1,n, interpret temporal distance 1 as one generation of proper time. What is the minimum number of colors or states needed so that any two events separated by proper time 1 must have different colors, i.e. what is χτ(R1,n) under this generational interpretation?

evidence.quote: A possible meaning of χτ (R1,n) is, e.g., that if we assume that we measure time in number of generations, then the events A and B corresponding to two immediately following generations should always be of different color.
In the relativistic case, as we have seen, two oscillating tastes are not enough, so how many do we need?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Minkowski space-time $\mathbb{R}^{1,n}$, i.e. $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ equipped with the quadratic form
$$Q(t,x_1,\dots,x_n) \;=\; t^2 - x_1^2 - \cdots - x_n^2.$$
For two events $A=(t_A,\mathbf{x}_A)$ and $B=(t_B,\mathbf{x}_B)$ with $Q(B-A) > 0$ (i.e. timelike separated), define the proper time between them as
$$\tau(A,B) \;=\; \sqrt{(t_B-t_A)^2 - \|\mathbf{x}_B-\mathbf{x}_A\|^2}.$$
Define the temporal chromatic number $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{1,n})$ to be the smallest cardinal $k$ such that there exists a coloring $c:\mathbb{R}^{1,n}\to\{1,2,\dots,k\}$ with the property that $c(A)\neq c(B)$ whenever $\tau(A,B)=1$.

Determine $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{1,n})$ for every integer $n\geq 1$. In particular, determine the minimum number of colors needed under the interpretation that proper time $1$ represents one generation, so that any two events separated by exactly one generation of proper time receive different colors.
artifact.status_search_result: The temporal/Lorentzian chromatic number of Minkowski space-time, where events at proper time distance 1 must be colored differently, is posed as an open problem. The classical Euclidean analogue (chromatic number of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with forbidden Euclidean distance 1) is a famous unsolved problem with only bounds known; the Minkowski/Lorentzian variant is even less studied. No exact value of $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{1,n})$ for general $n$ appears in the literature, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the space chromatic number
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the chromatic number of Euclidean space with one forbidden distance.
status_evidence.claim: Even the Euclidean analogue is open with only bounds known.

status_evidence.title: Colorings of R^n with several forbidden distances
status_evidence.snippet: Studies chromatic numbers of R^n with forbidden distance sets under various norms.
status_evidence.claim: The Lorentzian variant with proper-time forbidden distance is not resolved in this line of work.
